title: Rigveda 9.19: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.19: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.19 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 675v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.19.1-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 9); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 675v
translation.original_text:
1yat so̍ma ci̱tram u̱kthya̍ṁ di̱vyam pārthi̍va̱ṁ vasu̍ | tan na̍ḥ punā̱na ā bha̍ra ||
2yu̱vaṁ hi sthaḥ sva̍rpatī̱ indra̍ś ca soma̱ gopa̍tī | ī̱śā̱nā pi̍pyata̱ṁ dhiya̍ḥ ||
3vṛṣā̍ punā̱na ā̱yuṣu̍ sta̱naya̱nn adhi̍ ba̱rhiṣi̍ | hari̱ḥ san yoni̱m āsa̍dat ||
4avā̍vaśanta dhī̱tayo̍ vṛṣa̱bhasyādhi̱ reta̍si | sū̱nor va̱tsasya̍ mā̱tara̍ḥ ||
5ku̱vid vṛ̍ṣa̱ṇyantī̍bhyaḥ punā̱no garbha̍m ā̱dadha̍t | yāḥ śu̱kraṁ du̍ha̱te paya̍ḥ ||
6upa̍ śikṣāpata̱sthuṣo̍ bhi̱yasa̱m ā dhe̍hi̱ śatru̍ṣu | pava̍māna vi̱dā ra̱yim ||
7ni śatro̍ḥ soma̱ vṛṣṇya̱ṁ ni śuṣma̱ṁ ni vaya̍s tira | dū̱re vā̍ sa̱to anti̍ vā ||
translation.text:
1O SOMA, being purified bring us the wondrous treasure, meet For lauds, that is in earth and heaven.
2For ye Twain, Indra, Soma, are Lords of the light, Lords of the kine: Great Rulers, prosper ye our songs.
3The tawny Steer, while cleansed among the living, bellowing on the grass, Hath sunk and settled in his home.
4Over the Steer's productive flow the sacred songs were resonant, The mothers of the darling Son.
5Hath he not, purified, impregned the kine who long to meet their Lord, The kine who yield the shining milk?
6Bring near us those who stand aloof strike fear into our enemies: O Pavamâna, find us wealth.
7Soma, bring down the foeman's might, his vigorous strength and vital powe'r, Whether he be afar or near.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 675v (numbered 97v by the scribe) (OPenn image 676, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.18.5 ‹ime iti rodasī iti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 676r (numbered 98r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.20.1 ‹avyaḥ vārebhiḥ arṣati sahvān›. Verses 9.19.1-7 end on this page.
